hero.eyebrow: NIPUN Bharat · Foundational literacy and numeracy
hero.title: Every school visit should leave one clear next step.
hero.subtitle: Agla Kadam helps Cluster Resource Persons plan each week from an honest learning signal, coach teachers with evidence and check whether classroom practice actually changed.
hero.note: Works offline on low-cost phones and syncs automatically when a network is available.

loop.title: One loop, five steps
loop.subtitle: The mentor decides at every step. The platform does the reading, scoring, sorting and drafting.
loop.diagramLabel: The five-step mentoring loop: Pulse, Plan, Observe, Coach and Follow up, returning to Pulse.
loop.note: The loop closes when the next random check confirms the change.

pulse.title: Pulse
pulse.body: Each month the app randomly selects 20 children in every class of Classes 1 to 3 and releases five names a week. Teachers record a one-minute check inside the app: the child reads in the class's language, then speaks a little English. Children with special needs get an adapted check observed by the teacher.

plan.title: Plan
plan.body: Cluster Resource Persons receive a weekly visit plan ranked by learning gaps, pending follow-ups and block office orders.

observe.title: Observe
observe.body: Five focused observation items and a two-minute voice note replace long paper checklists.

coach.title: Coach
coach.body: Evidence-backed feedback, a ten-minute demonstration built on the day's textbook page and a space to rehearse the conversation.

followUp.title: Follow up
followUp.body: The next month's check shows whether the agreed step moved children's learning.

roles.title: Built for everyone who supports a classroom
roles.subtitle: Each role sees only what it needs, nothing more.

crp.title: Cluster Resource Persons
crp.body: A ranked weekly plan, a visit pack prepared in advance, structured observation and coaching tools.

teacher.title: Teachers
teacher.body: Five quick checks a week, attendance, practice cards, the school's own exams with marks, and class progress.

block.title: Block and district officers
block.body: Anonymised trends across clusters, never individual teacher records.

family.title: Students and parents
family.body: A child's own results and the learning material shared by the teacher.

principles.title: Designed for real classrooms
principles.subtitle: Rural schools have patchy networks, shared phones and very little time. Every design decision starts there.

offline.title: Works without a network
offline.body: Recordings and forms are encrypted on the device and uploaded automatically when a connection returns.

privacy.title: Children's privacy first
privacy.body: Audio only, with no photographs or biometrics. Recordings are deleted from the server within 30 days.

honest.title: Data no one can cherry-pick
honest.body: The system selects children at random. Teachers cannot choose, add or swap a child.

free.title: No licence fees
free.body: The platform runs on open-source models and free-tier infrastructure.

footer.alignment: Aligned with the NIPUN Bharat and Samagra Shiksha frameworks.
footer.privacy: Designed for the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.

guide.placement: Sit beside the child and hold the phone about 20 cm (one hand span) from the child's mouth.

guide.twoParts: The check has two parts in one minute. First the child reads a short text in {{language}} (about 40 seconds); if it is too hard, step down to words, then letters. Then the child talks about pictures in English.

consent.title: Consent for audio checks
consent.description: Pulse records only children whose parent or guardian has agreed.
consent.howItWorks: Give each family the consent form and record their decision here from the signed form. A family can change its mind at any time: record the new decision and it applies from then on. A child with consent takes part from the class's next draw: that night if the class has not been drawn this month, otherwise next month's, which is drawn on the 25th (after that, the month after).

tired-veteran.title: The experienced, tired teacher
tired-veteran.briefing: Kamla ji has taught for 24 years and teaches Classes 1 and 2 together, 38 children who come irregularly. In today's Hindi lesson the class repeated the story in chorus; the back rows did not open their books.
tired-veteran.opening: Come, sit. You saw it yourself. Half of them do not even come every day. What will a new method do?

eager-new-teacher.title: The eager new teacher
eager-new-teacher.briefing: Pooja is in her second year, alone with 52 children in Class 2. Today she covered two pages quickly; the same four children answered every question while many could not read the words.
eager-new-teacher.opening: Namaste! How did you find the class today? I tried to finish both lessons. Whatever you suggest, I will do all of it.

pulse-defensive.title: After a hard Pulse result
pulse-defensive.briefing: This month's Pulse heard 9 of the 20 sampled children in Ramesh ji's Class 3 reading at the lowest level. You have come to talk about it; he feels judged.
pulse-defensive.opening: That recording check of yours... the children were scared, and it is harvest time, half of them are in the fields. How is that my fault?

overloaded-head-teacher.title: The overloaded head teacher
overloaded-head-teacher.briefing: Yadav ji heads a two-teacher school and also teaches Class 3. Today his children copied from the board for most of the period while he filled registers.
overloaded-head-teacher.opening: Look, the midday meal accounts, the online data, and then the BEO's meetings... where is the time left to teach? You tell me.

teacher.intro: You are {{teacher}}, the teacher of Classes 2 and 3 at {{school}}.
teacher.step1: Take today's attendance for Class 2: tap the children who are absent.
teacher.step2: Open this week's Pulse: record a child reading the passage (allow the microphone), or see the children already checked.
teacher.step3: Enter the Maths marks of this month's class test, then share the latest monthly assessment with Class 2's families.
teacher.step4: Send a homework note to the families of Class 2.
teacher.step5: Open Progress for a class to see how each child's reading has moved since the session began.

crp.intro: You are {{crp}}, the CRP of the Rampur cluster's eight schools, {{school}} among them.
crp.step1: See this week's plan: which classes to visit first, and why.
crp.step2: Open a class pack before a visit: the Pulse trend, the step agreed last time, and recordings to listen to.
crp.step3: Verify the two children {{teacher}} added to Class 2 this week.
crp.step4: Start a visit: tap moments as the lesson goes on, answer four focus items, and agree one step with the teacher.
crp.step5: Ask Sahayak to draft and score your feedback, or rehearse a difficult conversation in the rehearsal room.
crp.step6: Open My coaching to see how your feedback and its follow-ups have changed over the months.

officer.intro: You are {{officer}}, the block education officer of Rampur block's sixteen schools.
officer.step1: See whether mentoring is changing practice: the follow-up visits that found the agreed step in use.
officer.step2: Compare Class 2 and Class 3 reading against NIPUN Bharat's Lakshya, month by month.
officer.step3: Notice what is held back: the English-medium classes are too few to show without singling a school out.

family.intro: You are the family of {{child}}, in Class 2 at {{school}}.
family.step2: Read the teacher's notes and homework.
family.step3: See the monthly assessment results the teacher shared.
family.step4: Practise reading and numbers together with the read-aloud games.
